label: Fentanyl PK — Shafer (1990)

parameters.label: central volume
parameters.covariate_model: V1 = 6.09 L (absolute; Shafer 1990 standard adult, valid ~40-90 kg)

extraction.tier_rationale: Source-filled from open reproductions of the Shafer 1990 STANPUMP fentanyl set (opentiva micro-rate constants k10 0.0827, k12 0.471, k13 0.225, k21 0.102, k31 0.006 -> V1 6.09; cross-checked vs the OpenTCI/Mandel MATLAB volume/clearance arrays). Absolute (not weight-scaled) in the canonical adult parameterization.

known_failure_modes.condition: total body weight >= 85 kg (Shibutani 2004 obese group: TBW >= 85 kg, BMI > 30)
known_failure_modes.behavior: The Shafer volumes/clearances are absolute (not scaled to body weight), but doses are given per kg of total body weight; Shibutani 2004 found the Shafer model systematically OVERESTIMATES measured plasma fentanyl as weight rises (performance error vs TBW R^2 = 0.689). Clearance tracks a nonlinear 'pharmacokinetic mass' (near-linear, slope ~0.65, below 100 kg; plateau ~100-108 kg above 140 kg), not TBW.

extraction.tier_rationale: Parameters SOURCE-FILLED (V1 6.09, V2 28.1, V3 228 L; Cl1 0.504, Cl2 2.87, Cl3 1.37 L/min; ke0 0.147) from two independent open reproductions of the Shafer 1990 STANPUMP fentanyl set (opentiva micro-rate constants and the OpenTCI/Mandel MATLAB arrays, which agree to displayed precision). KERNEL WIRED (fentanyl_shafer_1990) computing exactly these sourced constants, as rocuronium Wierda was: simulation is enabled while review_status stays pending_human_review — a human still confirms the primary table and resolves the ke0 split before promotion. Absolute (not weight-scaled) for the standard 40-90 kg adult; the Shafer 'pharmacokinetic mass' adjustment applies above ~80 kg.

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched two open implementations of the Shafer 1990 fentanyl model and reconciled their micro-rate constants / volume-clearance arrays to the displayed precision
sources: https://github.com/StevenLShafer/stanpumpR (R/drugs_fentanyl.R: notes Shafer 1990's own pooled model is V1 6.09 L, CL 0.504 L/min; tPeak 3.6 min from Shafer & Varvel 1991, Fig 2)
source_review.notes: V1 6.09, V2 28.1, V3 228 L and Cl1 0.504, Cl2 2.87, Cl3 1.37 L/min agree across both sources (opentiva micro-rate constants k10 0.0827/k12 0.471/k13 0.225/k21 0.102/k31 0.006 reduce exactly to the OpenTCI volume/clearance arrays). ke0: 0.147 (OpenTCI/Mandel, the curated value) vs 0.12 (opentiva) — a real implementation split, flagged. Specifically the SHAFER set, distinct from the Scott/McClain fentanyl models. Primary Anesthesiology PDF paywalled (not directly read). HUMAN ITEMS: confirm against the primary table, and resolve the ke0 0.147-vs-0.12 split. EVIDENCE FOR THE SPLIT (2026-11-16): stanpumpR independently confirms V1 6.09 L / CL 0.504 L/min and uses a 3.6-min time to peak effect (Shafer & Varvel 1991). On THESE kinetics that tpeak needs ke0 ~0.117/min; opentiva's 0.12 gives 3.55 min, while the curated 0.147 gives 3.17 min. That points to 0.147 belonging to a different kinetic set. Value left unchanged; a human decides. (Kernel since wired to these sourced constants, pending_human_review — the rocuronium precedent.)

notes: Parameters source-filled from open Shafer-1990 reproductions (pending_human_review); the kernel (fentanyl_shafer_1990) computes exactly those sourced constants with ke0 0.147/min (OpenTCI; opentiva codes 0.12). Obesity overprediction (Shibutani 2004) is an encoded failure mode. The volumes/clearances are absolute (standard adult). sufentanil (Gepts 1995) is now a sibling record; alfentanil (Maitre) is a future one.
